text: TaskUtils works. But working is a lower bar than ready for a teammate to rely on. This final lesson runs a real code review on the finished class, checks a production usage example, and closes out the entire course.

A real review checks finished code against specific pitfalls, not a vague does-this-look-okay pass. First, GlideRecord performance from Chapter 3: the membership query uses setLimit of one, and neither query sits inside a loop. Second, strict equality from Chapter 1: every comparison in the class, and in the Client Script that calls it, uses triple equals, never a loose double equals. Third, logging from Chapter 6: there's exactly one gs.info call in the whole class, and it only fires on the abnormal path. Fourth, every method guards its inputs so none of them can throw on incomplete data.

Here's the one comparison this review would flag if it had been written loosely: answer double-equals the string true. Loose equality could match other truthy-looking values in ways that quietly mask a bug. The fix is answer triple-equals true, an exact match. Right below it, the only logging call in the entire class - and notice it only runs inside the if block where the field turned out to be invalid, never on the normal successful path.

Here's how a real Business Rule in production calls this finished class. It creates a TaskUtils instance, calls isUserInGroup with the assigned user and a group name, and calls formatDueDate on the record's due date field. The priority check compares current dot getValue of priority against the string one, using triple equals - because GlideRecord field values always come back as strings, never as numbers. This Business Rule never reimplements the group lookup or date formatting itself; it just calls the two methods TaskUtils already got right, once.

Across three lessons, TaskUtils grew from three planned signatures into a real, working, reviewed Script Include. Other scripts across the instance can now call it instead of each reinventing the same GlideRecord query, the same date comparison, and the same reference field read. Written once, reviewed once, trusted everywhere - that's the actual point of a Script Include.

This course stayed deliberately low-level: variables, server-side scripting, GlideRecord, GlideAjax, client-side g_form, and debugging - the JavaScript a ServiceNow developer writes line by line. The next course in this path, ServiceNow Scripting and Application Development, builds full scoped applications - tables, UI policies, workflows, and reusable Script Includes like this one - on top of every skill you've built here.
